source_text: Properties of morphisms smooth local on source-and-target

<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces. There is an
intuitive meaning to the phrase ``<MATH_0002> is smooth local on the
source and target''. However, it turns out that this notion is not
the same as asking <MATH_0003> to be both smooth
local on the source and smooth local on the target.
We have discussed a similar phenomenon (for the <ACCENT_0001>tale topology and
the category of schemes) in great detail in
Descent, Section <REF_0001>
(for a quick overview take a look at
Descent, Remark <REF_0002>).
However, there is an important difference between the case of the smooth
and the <ACCENT_0002>tale topology. To see this difference we encourage the reader
to ponder the difference between
Descent, Lemma <REF_0003>
and
Lemma <REF_0004>
as well as the difference between
Descent, Lemma <REF_0005>
and
Lemma <REF_0006>.
Namely, in the <ACCENT_0003>tale setting the choice of the <ACCENT_0004>tale ``covering'' of the
target is immaterial, whereas in the smooth setting it is not.
